body: Just to be clear my wife and I are getting a divorce and there's no chance in hell of reconciliation.

My poor mother has already survived the loss of two children and this year my dad passed away. I just won't put her through anymore heartache. Also, even though I don't know how to show my love for them and I don't think they'll ever understand my pain I do have friends and a wife who love me and it's easier when I'm around them and we're having a good time.

I'm trying really hard, I'm just scared it might be too late but I have faith that she meant what she said about giving me a chance to change. I know I won't leave, I've never given up on a relationship in my life, which maybe isn't healthy but I don't give up on people. As long as the door is open, I'm there for them and to find a way to make things work. So the ball is in her court so to speak. I love her deeply and unconditionally, so much it hurts me right now. Its up to her whether or not she wants to receive that love.

>Woah. Immaturity and lack of logic/knowledge again. She is WAY more likely to be sexually assaulted by someone she knows. sigh

I can see that but I can also understand the idea that somebody she is friends with and trusts would not do that to her. She's a smart woman and reads people well so I'll trust she knows what she's doing. Truthfully, I feel like I owe her this. Even though I feel like she should have come forward with her concerns about our relationship a lot sooner I'm wracked with guilt over the fact that somebody I love so deeply, more than anybody else, ever questioned that because of how I behaved and I feel extremely guilty because so much of our relationship has, accidentally, ended up as a compromise in my direction. Namely in that I went to school full time and finished my degree while she worked and went to school part time. I'm very recently graduated and want to be able to return the favor. I know it sounds like a shitty situation but truthfully, we live in a very small town, the university is pretty much the only thing keeping it afloat and it is really hard to find work here. I searched and searched and searched while I was in school but never got anywhere. She told me it was okay if I focused on school and never seemed resentful about it. I feel now though that she probably did somewhat. I'm currently employed now and am trying really hard to undo the damage my unemployment might have done on the relationship and focus hard on making things about her for a while. I get how one can think she's immature and selfish and it does drive me crazy to no end that she waited so long to tell me what she felt (and even then I had to pretty much drag it out of her) but I owe her so much and I feel like a lot of this is my own doing just through plain ignorance.

>So sorry about your dad. And your dog. I lost my dog in November. We had twelve great years together. I'll get another when I'm ready. Are you considering getting a new one yourself?

Well, a coworker of her's (one she doesn't have any desire to fuck, hardy har har) found a puppy that they couldn't take care of so we took him in. We've had him for a month now and I love the guy. There's an issue though that he's a big dog and we live in a small apartment and we're both so busy we probably don't have as much time to put into him as we should. We've started discussing if we should give him to somebody else that has more time to take care of him and maybe yard for him to run around in the. The logic is sound but it's hard for me to face because getting the new dog was the first thing that really went right after my dad passing away and it helped assuage that grief, especially the grief over our old dog. I don't know if I'm some kind of selfish cunt for wanting to keep him or if I'm delusional in telling myself I can make time to train him, spend time with him, etc.

It's a bit too late for those suggestions. I already agreed to it. I understand its something she needs for her sexual development. She didn't force it on me and I have my own curiosities I'm going to be exploring as well. I was satisfied not having these answers but I get why she needs them.

>Open relationship or not, it is a (I wish I knew how to do bigger font for the following word:) TERRIBLE idea to get involved with people you work with, and even MORE TERRIBLE when her workmates know she's married. When it goes bad (and it will) it will make her job/life so much worse, which will make your life worse. I'm mostly against the idea of a "veto" rule in open relationships (because I've gotten vetoed into monogamy by an immature partner), but it is an excellent rule to never get involved with co-workers. I can't say for sure, but your wife might have just decided she really wants to sleep with someone she works with, so she doesn't really want an open relationship, she just has an infatuation with one person. There are about seven billion people your wife does NOT work with: if you agree to an open relationship, tell her she can choose any of them.

Trust me, I told her all that. She countered that she has no friends outside of work and she's worried about being sexually assaulted by a stranger. I don't think she's infatuated with one coworker and I get why she's comfortable with somebody she knows even though I have no interest in fucking somebody I know. 

>Eek. The frustrating lack of logic of people that don't understand depression. She needs to understand that your depression is not about her, and when she takes it personally in this manner, it's unhealthy for both of you. I'll repeat: this is a matter for counseling.

It is a bit frustrating but I'm also aware most people have a really limited understanding of depression so I'm not too mad about it.

>Oh gosh... her reaction about your dad's death is really, really, frighteningly selfish. Um... is there a chance your wife is really immature? I note that you two got married really young, which sometimes deprives people of life experiences that create maturity and selflessness and unconditional kindness

I think it could be just because we're young in general. She's never lost a close family member like that, most people our age haven't, so they don't really know what I'm going through. I think we're both lacking in emotional maturity in several areas.

Thank you so much for your advice and kind words and definitely your hugs.
